meta.covers: General breach notification laws of the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, plus five federal and international rules, as understood on the last_updated date.
meta.legal_disclaimer: For planning and education only. This is not legal advice. Laws change and contain exceptions this file does not capture. Confirm every deadline with counsel.

data_types.driver_license: Driver's license or state ID number
data_types.financial: Financial account or payment card number with an access code or password
data_types.biometric: Biometric data (fingerprint, face or retina scan)
data_types.credentials: Username or e-mail address with a password or security answer

meta.source_note: State entries were compiled from secondary summaries published in October and November 2026 and were not checked line by line against each statute.

sector_rules.name: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
sector_rules.applies_to: HIPAA covered entities and business associates, for unsecured protected health information.

obligations.text: Without unreasonable delay, no later than 60 calendar days after discovery.

obligations.who: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
obligations.text: For 500 or more individuals: at the same time as individual notice, no later than 60 days after discovery. Smaller breaches are reported to HHS annually.
Required when more than 500 residents of one state or jurisdiction are affected. Check the count per state.

sector_rules.name: SEC cybersecurity incident disclosure (Form 8-K, Item 1.05)
sector_rules.applies_to: Companies that file reports with the SEC.

obligations.who: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (public filing)
obligations.text: Within 4 business days after the company determines the incident is material. The date shown assumes materiality was determined on the discovery date.

sector_rules.name: FTC Safeguards Rule notification
sector_rules.applies_to: Non-bank financial institutions under the FTC's jurisdiction (for example lenders, dealers, tax preparers).

obligations.text: Within 30 days of discovery when unencrypted information of 500 or more consumers is involved.

sector_rules.name: EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
sector_rules.applies_to: Organizations subject to GDPR when personal data of people in the EU is involved.

obligations.who: Your lead EU data protection authority
obligations.text: Within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to individuals. The date shown is 3 days after discovery; count the exact hours yourself.
Without undue delay, when the breach is likely to result in a high risk to them.

sector_rules.name: CIRCIA cyber incident reporting
sector_rules.law: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022
sector_rules.applies_to: Critical infrastructure entities, once the rule is final.
sector_rules.status_text: Not yet required. CISA sent the final rule for White House review on October 1, 2026 and it had not been published as of November 12, 2026. When it takes effect it is expected to require reports to CISA within 72 hours of a covered incident and 24 hours of a ransom payment. Check cisa.gov/circia.
